span.label: Because of the way neurophysiological data must be recorded and the equipment required, neuroscience-based economic experiments are confined mostly to questions about individual human beings rather than groups or markets.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: EEG's very good temporal resolution makes it the tool of choice for tracking how brain activity changes over time and for analysing reactions to external stimuli.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: fMRI localises activity by showing how much oxygen is delivered to specific parts of the brain, which is what EEG cannot do.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: fMRI buys very good spatial resolution at the price of an examination procedure that is cumbersome for the participant.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Neurophysiological measurement can be more faithful to what participants actually do than self-report measures are.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Substantial information processing in the brain that drives economic decisions cannot be observed at all through behavioural research methods.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Experiments using transmagnetic stimulation establish a causal relationship between brain activity and economic choice that is independent of environmental factors.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Neuroscience techniques can surface fundamental principles of decision making - such as the effect of physical environment, mood or cultural background - that traditional economic research treated as irrelevant.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Every later model of the decision process still contains Simon's three phases of intelligence, design and choice, differing only in naming and in how finely the phases are split.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Behavioural experiments can document that people deviate from expected utility theory, but only cognitive neuroscience can supply the explanation of why they are not as rational as the theory assumes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Both the decision-making and the cognitive neuroscience literatures have concentrated on the final phase of the process - evaluation and choice - leaving the intelligence and design phases comparatively unstudied.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The cost of the specialised equipment, fMRI above all, is one of the practical obstacles to using neuroscience in economic experiments.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A single cognitive neuroscience experiment yields an enormous amount of neurophysiological data, which forces the use of very sophisticated analysis methods.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
